sources.entry: pyfiglet - An implementation of figlet written in Python.

summary.one_liner: pyfiglet is a pure-Python port of FIGlet that renders text as ASCII art using FIGlet-style fonts, usable as a library or command-line tool.
summary.what_it_does: Takes plain text and renders it in ASCII art fonts such as the 'block' and 'slant' styles. It is a port of the FIGlet C program, with kerning and smushing logic translated to Python, and the README says output should match FIGlet. It can be called from Python code via a Figlet class or a figlet_format function, or run from the command line with options similar to C figlet, where -f selects the font (default standard.flf). Fonts can be installed from a single font file or a ZIP archive of many fonts using the -L option. On Unix-like systems it also finds fonts installed by FIGlet in /usr/local/share/figlet and /usr/share/figlet. Toilet (.tlf) fonts are included, imported from toilet 0.3-1.
use_cases: Render text as ASCII art banners in a terminal
Generate figlet-style headers inside a Python program
Add decorative text titles to command-line tool output
Use FIGlet fonts without running an external figlet program
Install custom figlet or toilet font files for reuse
how_to_run: pip install pyfiglet (implied by packaging; README does not show this command explicitly)
pyfiglet -f slant 'text to render' (font selection via -f, per README)
from pyfiglet import Figlet; f = Figlet(font='slant'); print(f.renderText('text to render'))
import pyfiglet; print(pyfiglet.figlet_format('text to render', font='slant'))
pyfiglet -L <fontfile-or-zip> to install a font (may need sudo)
notable: Pure-Python port of FIGlet with output intended to match the original C program, including kerning and smushing
Usable both as a Python library and as a command-line tool
Can read fonts from ZIP archives so a whole font collection lives in one file
Reuses system FIGlet font directories on Unix-like systems
caveats: Some fonts were removed from distribution due to licensing concerns; the README points to a separate location for them
Font installation with -L may require root access depending on how pyfiglet was installed
The README describes the smushing/kerning code as fragile and complex
